Hi @comwanga. Thanks for working on this :)

This is a big, complex and scary PR. 3.2k lines makes it really hard to review properly, and the fix #2687 asks for looks way smaller than that. I wonder if its worth splitting into smaller chunks, something like:

1) the actual fix: keep the saga pending when restore finds nothing, and only complete an orphan saga from validated outputs. Only `resume.rs` + the regression tests, no trait changes, so it could even be backported to 0.18.x
2) `finalize_receive` + `atomic_settlement`
3) `restore_proofs`

The redb missing saga table commit, the terminal transaction status on upsert and the duplicate signature check look independent, so they could be separate PRs and get merged right away.

Also, maybe dumb question, but what does `restore_proofs` buy us over always checking output states with the mint during recovery? I think most of the `atomic_settlement` machinery exists to skip that NUT-07 call, and it pushes a pretty big contract onto every storage adapter (custom and FFI ones included). I'd rather discuss that in its own issue before reviewing it.

Cross-system context that might be useful: we looked at how other systems handle change delivery on async settlement. Lightning fuses change into the channel update itself (no separate retrieval channel exists to break). Fedimint returns change notes in the peg-out response. Stripe's pattern is to build the complete result once and serve it identically on every retrieval. In each case the design principle is the same: the completion event and the value it carries arrive together, on every path. We mention this only because it informed our reading of NUT-08's MUST-return language — not as a prescription for the fix.

Thanks for the pointer. To be precise for anyone landing here: the **published crates.io release (cdk-ffi 0.18.2) — the version current cdk-go natives are built from — has no Drop impl**; the repro is against that release, so hosts on today's binaries still hit this. Two notes on the fix shape in case they're useful: (1) our measured failure also occurs with `shutdown_background`-style paths when sqlx pool tasks are still live on the runtime (shutdown races them and can abort) — which is why we chose `mem::forget` (leak) in our verified patch: bounded, a few threads per long-lived wallet object, no shutdown window at all; (2) we verified the leak-Drop across x86-64 and 32-bit MIPS (mips + mipsel) with a full wallet acceptance suite (mint/round-trip/melt/drain), checksums unchanged. If a release including the fix is planned, a note here would help FFI hosts know when to re-pin — happy to re-verify our suite against it.

Thanks for the review! Fixed in 1140e5dc: relays from an `r` tag are now collected from every value (`tag[1..]`) and deduplicated against the nprofile relays, so nothing after the first value is dropped.

Added a regression test in 45c9d765 with a relay-free nprofile and `["r", "wss://first.example", "wss://second.example"]`, checking that both relays survive encoding and two round trips.

Thanks for the review! Addressed both points:

- 1c4a3a75: the npub check now compares with `Hrp` equality, which ignores case, so an all-uppercase `NPUB1…` takes the npub path. Added a test that the lowercase and uppercase forms produce identical CREQ-B output.
- de6e68cf: npub targets are decoded with `CheckedHrpstring::new::<Bech32>`, so a Bech32m-encoded npub is now rejected with a checksum error. Added a test for that.

I left the decoder npub/nprofile representation as is, so it can go in a separate PR as you suggested.

Thanks, good catch! Pending and already-signed outputs are now kept apart:

- f6c658ab adds `Error::OutputsPending` (11004) and a `database::Error::BlindedMessagePending` that maps to it.
- df58191b: `add_blinded_messages` checks for existing rows before inserting. A signed row (`c IS NOT NULL`) still returns `Duplicate` (11003); a reservation with `c IS NULL` returns `BlindedMessagePending`. A concurrent insert is still caught by the constraint as before.
- 9f7381bb maps `BlindedMessagePending` to `OutputsPending` in `map_add_blinded_messages_error` and in the swap saga mapping.
- Tests: a shared mint DB test (9393028b), plus a swap regression test (0ebbf23e) that leaves the first swap set up but unsigned and then submits a second swap with the same outputs, expecting 11004.

The existing 11003 tests for swap, mint and melt still pass.

Mutation + PostgreSQL testing on `0ebbf23e`. Two commits (tests, then fix): https://github.com/Codepocketdev/cdk/tree/2786-pending-tests

1. **warning** Overlapping requests still get 11003 for an unsigned output: the pre-check SELECTs can't see the other open tx's row, so the insert hits `Duplicate`. Fails 6/6 on PostgreSQL. Fix: `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, then read the row.
2. **warning** No 11004 test for mint, batch mint or melt change: mapping the pending arm in `verification.rs` to 11003 keeps all `cdk` tests green.

Repro: `cargo test -p cdk-postgres --lib concurrent_reservation` fails on f27c27a3, passes on 4a6f66ee.

Checked main again (fetch today): crates/cdk-ffi/src/runtime.rs still has no Drop impl — git grep 'impl Drop' origin/main -- crates/cdk-ffi/src/ returns only nwc.rs:84 NwcService, and the last commit touching runtime.rs (9c72cb9b, 'Consolidate FFI runtime handling into RuntimeGuard') consolidates construction but adds no drop handling. A direct empirical re-test against main's built .so isn't possible from the Go side yet — main's FFI surface has moved past the 0.18.2-generated bindings (e.g. tokenurdecoder, walletrepository_new_with_config), so it won't link without regeneration. This is therefore source-level; will re-run the runtime suite once a release cuts.

Thanks for following up. `cdk-ffi` **0.18.3**, published October 29, includes the `RuntimeGuard::drop` fix from #2581, backported in #2731. I also checked the published crate archive and confirmed the implementation is present. Current `main` contains it as well.

#2761 separately hardens SQL transaction cleanup and is also included in 0.18.3.

Please retest with native binaries built from 0.18.3 and matching generated bindings. If the failure persists, please share a minimal reproducer, full backtrace, and the exact native library version/source SHA. That would let us investigate whether there’s a remaining lifetime issue beyond the runtime-drop panic already addressed.

@Codepocketdev thanks for testing this on PostgreSQL, both points were real.

1. dc2df883 drops the pre-check SELECTs and inserts with `ON CONFLICT (blinded_message) DO NOTHING`, which waits for the other transaction. If nothing was inserted, one query over the request's outputs decides: any signed output gives `Duplicate` (11003), otherwise `BlindedMessagePending` (11004). That also keeps 11003 when a request mixes signed and pending outputs (test in e610707a). f424f055 adds a PostgreSQL test with an open reservation in a second transaction; it fails on the previous head and passes now.
2. 37757fce and e49ae5d4 add 11004 tests for single mint, batch mint and melt change outputs. Mapping the pending arm in `verification.rs` to 11003 now fails all three.

Locally: cdk-postgres 150/150, cdk-sqlite 149/149, cdk `mint::` 260/260, clippy clean.
